title: Security Research Engineer, AI Safety and Security Engineering
body: nvidia, widely recognized as one of the world’s most desirable employers, believes open-weight models are foundational to american ai leadership, cybersecurity, and defense through broad scientific scrutiny. as part of this mission, our ai safety & security engineering team builds and evaluates ai-powered tooling that finds, validates, and patches software vulnerabilities, recognizing that finding a bug is only the beginning. we are seeking a security research engineer to advance our validate and patch capabilities by establishing what counts as a confirmed vulnerability and defining what constitutes a truly correct, safe fix. in this critical role, you will apply rigorous security judgment to well-defined categories of vulnerabilities. these affect nvidia-internal targets. you will turn complex analysis into repeatable methods that improve software people rely on daily. validation here requires meticulous care to confirm reports are real and reachable rather than noise, while patching requires ensuring fixes repair flaws, protect existing behavior, and hold up under strict revalidation. working alongside harness and evaluation engineers, you will establish high engineering standards, document your reasoning for independent security reviews, and ensure your methods run reliably with fully traceable evidence. ai-assisted workflows are an integral part of this job, but so is maintaining a healthy, disciplined skepticism about their outputs. beyond immediate fixes, your work will teach the entire program what trustworthy patching looks like while actively helping decide which vulnerability classes the team tackles next. ultimately, we hold our results to an exceptionally high bar and value specific, verifiable proof of your technical expertise—such as cves, advisories, or original security tools—over polished phrasing. what you'll be doing: validation methods: develop techniques that confirm vulnerabilities are real and reachable. patch methods: advance approaches for generating and verifying safe fixes. quality standards: define correctness, regression, and revalidation standards with reviewers. applied research: work bounded vulnerability classes against internal targets. what we need to see: bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) with 12+ years in security research or software engineering. security foundations: hands-on vulnerability research, fuzzing, program analysis, or secure development in c, c++, or python. fix quality: rigor about what makes a fix correct and safe, including regression and behavior preservation. ai-assisted workflows: comfort using ai-assisted tools for analysis and development. ways to stand out from the crowd: public research: cves, advisories, or publications in vulnerability research. analysis tooling: experience building or extending fuzzers, static analyzers, or symbolic-execution tools. agentic ml: familiarity with llm-based coding or analysis agents. our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible. job description: the sector safety manager – federal & environmental programs provides strategic and operational safety, health & environmental (sh&e) leadership across a portfolio of federal, environmental, infrastructure, and field-based programs. this position partners with sector and program leadership to ensure effective implementation of parsons’ sh&e management system, contractual safety and environmental requirements, and applicable federal, state, and local regulations. the role serves as the primary sh&e partner to assigned sector leadership and provides oversight, technical guidance, assurance, and escalation support to project safety professionals and operational teams. particular emphasis is placed on federal contracting requirements, environmental compliance, high-hazard field activities, project mobilization, and proactive risk management . the sector safety manager is expected to operate beyond traditional compliance management by helping project teams identify risk early, develop practical solutions, improve execution, and integrate sh&e considerations into operational and business decisions. what you'll be doing sector sh&e leadership serve as the primary sh&e business partner for assigned sector leadership, program managers, project managers, and operational teams. translate parsons corporate sh&e strategy, policies, standards, and objectives into effective sector and project-level execution. provide oversight and technical direction to project safety personnel while maintaining strong alignment with operational leadership. monitor sector sh&e performance, identify emerging risks and trends, and develop targeted improvement strategies. participate in operational reviews, project risk discussions, leadership meetings, and other business forums where sh&e expertise is required. support development and execution of annual sector sh&e objectives, key performance indicators, assurance activities, and improvement plans. promote a learning-focused safety culture that emphasizes employee engagement, human and organizational performance principles, proactive risk identification, and prevention of serious injuries and fatalities. federal program safety provide sh&e leadership for projects performed for federal agencies, including programs subject to requirements established by agencies such as usace, dod, faa, dhs, epa, and other federal clients . interpret and support implementation of contractual sh&e requirements, including applicable provisions of em 385-1-1, osha regulations, far/dfars requirements, client-specific safety standards, and approved project accident prevention plans/safety plans . support project mobilization by reviewing contractual requirements and ensuring appropriate sh&e staffing, qualifications, plans, training, and controls are established before field activities begin. review project-specific accident prevention plans, activity hazard analyses, environmental plans, emergency response plans, and related sh&e documentation for quality and contractual compliance. assist operations with identification and qualification of required safety personnel, including sshos and other contractually mandated sh&e positions. partner with proposal and capture teams to identify sh&e requirements, staffing needs, risk considerations, and associated costs during pursuit and proposal development. support responses to client concerns, audits, findings, corrective actions, cure notices, and other sh&e-related contractual matters. environmental leadership provide advanced environmental compliance expertise to federal and commercial programs involving construction, remediation, environmental services, infrastructure, and field operations. interpret and support compliance with applicable environmental regulations and permit requirements, including rcra, cercla, cwa, caa, tsca, nepa, spcc, stormwater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, and state-specific environmental requirements . support projects involving environmental remediation, contaminated sites, hazardous materials, waste characterization, transportation and disposal, spill prevention, and environmental monitoring. review environmental work plans, compliance plans, permits, sampling activities, waste profiles, manifests, and related project documentation as appropriate. assist project teams in identifying environmental risks during proposal, planning, mobilization, and execution phases. partner with environmental technical professionals to ensure appropriate integration of environmental, health, and safety controls. support environmental incident response, regulatory notifications, corrective actions, and lessons learned. maintain awareness of regulatory developments and communicate significant changes and associated business impacts to sector leadership. risk management & operational support facilitate and support project risk assessments for higher-risk work and emerging operational hazards. evaluate project sh&e risk based on scope, geography, contractual requirements, environmental conditions, workforce exposure, and operational complexity. support implementation of parsons’ risk-ranking processes to ensure sh&e resources and assurance activities are focused on the highest-risk projects. partner with operational leadership to establish effective controls for high-risk activities. conduct field visits and leadership engagements to evaluate implementation of sh&e requirements and identify opportunities to improve operational performance. exercise appropriate stop-work authority when imminent danger or significant uncontrolled risk exists. assurance, incident management & performance lead or support sh&e audits, assessments, project reviews, and assurance activities across assigned programs. evaluate compliance with parsons requirements, client expectations, regulatory requirements, and project-specific sh&e plans. monitor corrective actions through effective and timely closure. support investigations of significant incidents and high-potential events using learning-focused investigation principles. evaluate underlying organizational, operational, and human factors rather than relying solely on individual behaviors or immediate causes. identify recurring themes across projects and translate lessons learned into sector-level preventive actions. monitor leading and lagging sh&e indicators and provide meaningful performance analysis to sector leadership. support timely and accurate incident reporting, investigation quality, regulatory reporting, and management review. employee & team development provide technical guidance, coaching, and mentoring to project safety managers, safety leads, sshos, environmental professionals, and other sh&e personnel. assess sh&e staffing and competency requirements based on project risk and contractual obligations. support recruitment, selection, onboarding, and development of qualified sh&e personnel. identify competency gaps and develop strategies to improve technical and leadership capabilities across the sector. foster collaboration among safety, environmental, operations, quality, hr, legal, risk, and other support functions. required qualifications bachelor’s degree in occupational safety, environmental science, environmental engineering, industrial hygiene, engineering, construction management , or a closely related discipline. typically 10+ years of progressive sh&e experience , with significant experience supporting federal, environmental, construction, engineering, remediation, or infrastructure operations. demonstrated experience supporting u.s. federal government contracts and projects . strong working knowledge of osha requirements and federal/client-specific sh&e requirements. significant experience with environmental compliance and/or environmental remediation operations . experience developing, reviewing, or implementing project-specific safety and environmental plans. demonstrated ability to interpret contractual and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational controls. experience conducting audits, risk assessments, incident investigations, and management reviews. demonstrated ability to influence project managers and senior operational leaders without relying solely on direct authority. strong written, verbal, analytical, and executive communication skills. ability to travel to project locations as required. preferred certified safety professional (csp), certified industrial hygienist (cih), certified hazardous materials manager (chmm), or equivalent professional certification. experience supporting usace/dod programs and em 385-1-1 requirements . current or previous ssho qualification under applicable federal requirements. 40-hour hazwoper and applicable supervisor-level hazwoper training. experience with environmental remediation, hazardous waste operations, cercla/rcra sites, or complex environmental programs. experience supporting large, geographically dispersed federal portfolios. experience with iso 14001 and/or iso 45001 management systems. experience supporting proposals, project startups, mobilizations, and federal contract compliance reviews. leadership expectations the sector safety manager is expected to function as an operational partner and technical leader , not solely as a compliance resource. success requires the ability to understand the business, recognize risk, engage effectively with project leadership, and provide practical solutions that enable safe and compliant execution. the successful candidate will: build credibility and trusted relationships with operational and project leadership. proactively engage projects rather than waiting for issues to escalate. challenge ineffective practices while maintaining a solutions-oriented approach. understand both contractual requirements and operational realities . hold project teams accountable while providing the resources and technical support necessary for success. use data, field observations, employee feedback, and operational intelligence to anticipate risk. promote learning and continuous improvement following incidents, near misses, and successful work. maintain consistent sh&e expectations across the sector while recognizing project-specific contractual and risk requirements. measures of success performance in this role will be evaluated through a combination of leading and lagging indicators, including: federal contract sh&e compliance and audit performance. environmental compliance performance and prevention of significant regulatory events. quality and timely closure of corrective actions. project mobilization readiness and quality of sh&e planning. effectiveness of high-risk project oversight. quality and timeliness of incident investigations. reduction in repeat events and significant/high-potential exposures. leadership engagement and operational stakeholder satisfaction. development and competency of assigned sh&e personnel. effective implementation of parsons sh&e programs, standards, and strategic initiatives. demonstrated contribution to safe, compliant, and successful project execution. role differentiation this position is differentiated from a traditional project safety manager by its portfolio-level accountability and breadth of technical responsibility . the sector safety manager provides oversight across multiple projects and programs, serves as the sh&e partner to sector leadership, and brings specialized expertise in federal contracting and environmental compliance . the role is expected to identify systemic risks, establish consistent expectations across projects, strengthen project sh&e capabilities, and ensure that parsons’ corporate sh&e strategy is effectively translated into operational execution throughout the sector. security clearance requirement: none this position is part of our corporate team. for over 80 years, parsons corporation, has shaped the future of the defense, intelligence, and critical infrastructure markets. our employees work in a close-knit team environment to find new, innovative ways to deliver smart solutions that are used and valued by customers around the world. by combining unique technologies with deep domain expertise across cybersecurity, missile defense, space, connected infrastructure, transportation, smart cities, and more, we're providing tomorrow's solutions today. salary range: $112,200.00 - $196,400.00 we value our employees and want our employees to take care of their overall wellbeing, which is why we offer best-in-class benefits such as medical, rigging, equipment, or related technical work. proven ability to organize personnel and work activities to meet project manpower, schedule, productivity, safety, and quality requirements. ability to read and understand engineering drawings, project plans, schedules, scopes of work, and other technical documentation. working knowledge of field construction and installation methods, practices, safety requirements, and quality-control processes. strong leadership, organizational, and communication skills. ability to coordinate effectively with field personnel, engineers, project managers, subcontractors, and customer representatives. must be willing to travel extensively and work at project sites throughout the united states as required. must be able to meet customer security requirements. a background check by federal authorities will be performed. what desired skills you’ll bring: experience supporting large civil, structural, industrial, electrical, mechanical, or technical field projects. experience supervising electricians, electronics technicians, installers, field engineers, craft personnel, or other multi-discipline field crews. experience with equipment removal, disposition, decommissioning, installation, site preparation, or site restoration activities. experience supporting faa, aviation, air traffic control, radar, surveillance, communications, or other mission-critical infrastructure. familiarity with faa facilities, national airspace system infrastructure, or other active operational environments. experience coordinating subcontractors and title: SCA UXO Tech II (deploy to Guam)
body: in a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. imagine next! at parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible. job description: are you interested in making the world a safer place through your expertise and experience with unexploded ordnance (uxo)? if so, parsons has an opportunity for you! we need your help with the reconnaissance, classification, and removal of uxo from affected communities. responsibilities: perform the duties of a uxo technician ii as outlined in ddesb tp 18. (a) meet the criteria for and perform the functions of a uxo-ti. (b) store explosive materials in accordance with applicable guidance, including preparing on-site holding areas to temporarily store and secure mec or mppeh and other explosives (e.g., donor charges). (c) determine, using a variety of techniques (e.g., global positioning equipment, land navigation techniques), and record the location of subsurface anomalies, surface mec, and other material of interest in a field environment. (d) perform field collection and testing procedures to identify explosives contaminated media or material (e.g., equipment used for the load-assemble-pack of military munitions). (e) inspect and document the explosives safety status of mppeh. (f) supervise, as required, sws, sp, and uxo-tis. uxo technician i duties: (a) investigate for and identify mec and mppeh, including explosive residues in media (e.g., soil), buildings, and installed equipment. (b) identify different types of military munitions, including identifying whether a military munition’s fuse is armed or unarmed. (c) excavate subsurface anomalies for identification. (d) move (e.g., consolidate) mec within a munitions response site (mrs) or on an operational range after the uxoso and suxos have jointly evaluated and documented the determination that the risk of movement is acceptable. (e) operate vehicles moving explosives or mppeh on site. individuals must be appropriately licensed for the class of vehicle being operated. (f) transport military munitions, commercial explosives, and mdeh that meets the criteria in paragraphs 2.2.b.(1)(a) through (e) and has been determined safe for transport over public traffic routes (ptrs). such munitions and explosives must be packaged in a manner that allows their safe transport and complies with department of transportation (dot) and other applicable federal and state laws and dod policies. only uxo determined to be safe for transport by eod personnel may be transported over a ptr. (g) prepare electric and non-electric firing systems. (h) set up decontamination stations and decontaminate ca-contaminated personnel, military munitions, and other material of interest (e.g., munitions debris, glass vials) in accordance with approved plans. performing these functions may require additional training. (i) assist uxoqp in documenting the explosives safety status of mppeh. (j) construct engineering controls (protective works). qualifications: 3+ years of experience as a uxo technician i or graduate of military eod school. ***job location is guam*** security clearance requirement: none this position is part of our federal solutions team. the federal solutions segment delivers resources to our us government customers that ensure the success of missions around the globe. our intelligent employees drive the state of the art as they provide services and solutions in the areas of defense, security, intelligence, infrastructure, and environmental. we promote a culture of excellence and close-knit teams that take pride in delivering, protecting, and sustaining our nation's most critical assets, from earth to cyberspace. throughout the company, our people are anticipating what’s next to deliver the solutions our customers need now. salary range: $15.68 - $71.30 this position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will continue to be posted for an average of 30 days until a qualified applicant is selected or the position has been cancelled. parsons is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other protected status. we truly invest and care about our employee’s wellbeing and provide endless growth opportunities as the sky is the limit, so aim for the stars! imagine next and join the parsons quest—apply today! parsons is aware of fraudulent recruitment practices. to learn more about recruitment fraud and how to report it, please refer to https://www.parsons.com/fraudulent-recruitment/ .

title: SCA UXO Tech III (deploy to Guam)
body: in a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. imagine next! at parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible. job description: are you interested in making the world a safer place through your expertise and experience with unexploded ordnance (uxo)? if so, parsons has an opportunity for you! we need your help with the reconnaissance, classification, and removal of uxo from affected communities. responsibilities: perform the duties of a uxo technician iii as outlined in ddesb tp 18. uxo-tiiis must be able to: (a) meet the criteria for, and perform the functions of, a uxo-ti and uxo-tii. (b) ensure compliance with dod military service- and/or ddesb-approved site plans. (c) supervise and perform on-site destruction or demilitarization of mec in place or at a consolidated detonation site. this includes determining where and when it is safe to initiate destruction and when engineering controls are required to mitigate the effects of a detonation. (d) implement an explosives storage plan in accordance with applicable guidance. (e) prepare administrative reports required for munitions responses (e.g., daily uxo team report), operational range clearance activities, and similar operations. (f) develop and implement standard operating procedures and work plans for munitions responses and operational range clearance activities. (g) assist in the preparation of risk and hazard analyses. (h) conduct daily site safety briefings. (i) supervise mec-related activities performed at a site. (j) determine if mdeh, which is not known or suspected to be uxo, is safe to ship and properly documented for transport over ptrs in accordance with technical bulletin 700-2, naval sea systems command instruction 8020.8c, technical order 11a-1-47. (k) package military munitions, commercial explosives, and mdeh that has been determined safe for transport over ptrs. (l) serve as the uxo team leader. uxo i and ii (b) store explosive materials in accordance with applicable guidance, including preparing on-site holding areas to temporarily store and secure mec or mppeh and other explosives (e.g., donor charges). (c) determine, using a variety of techniques (e.g., global positioning equipment, land navigation techniques), and record the location of subsurface anomalies, surface mec, and other material of interest in a field environment. (d) perform field collection and testing procedures to identify explosives contaminated media or material (e.g., equipment used for the load-assemble-pack of military munitions). (e) inspect and document the explosives safety status of mppeh. (f) supervise, as required, sws, sp, and uxo-tis. uxo technician i duties: (a) investigate for and identify mec and mppeh, including explosive residues in media (e.g., soil), buildings, and installed equipment. (b) identify different types of military munitions, including identifying whether a military munition’s fuze is armed or unarmed. (c) excavate subsurface anomalies for identification. (d) move (e.g., consolidate) mec within a munitions response site (mrs) or on an operational range after the uxoso and suxos have jointly evaluated and documented the determination that the risk of movement is acceptable. (e) operate vehicles moving explosives or mppeh on site. individuals must be appropriately licensed for the class of vehicle being operated. (f) transport military munitions, commercial explosives, and mdeh that meets the criteria in paragraphs 2.2.b.(1)(a) through (e) and has been determined safe for transport over public traffic routes (ptrs). such munitions and explosives must be packaged in a manner that allows their safe transport and complies with department of transportation (dot) and other applicable federal and state laws and dod policies. only uxo determined to be safe for transport by eod personnel may be transported over a ptr. (g) prepare electric and non-electric firing systems. title: SCA UXO Safety Officer (deploy to Guam)
body: in a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. imagine next! at parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible. job description: ready to put your skills to work on technical or engineering projects? are you great with people and have willingness to work hard to get the job done? parsons is seeking a candidate with a desire to enhance the fabric of our community. role: the uxo safety officer works as a lead uxo safety specialist on site. a candidate must have at least 10 years eod/mec experience if an eod school graduate, or 13 years if a graduate of a uxo technician i school. there are other time and experience level requirements associated with this position. reference dod tp 18 dtd 24 june 2020. in accordance with department of defense technical paper 18, a suxos must: (a) meet the criteria for, and perform the functions of, a uxo-tiii, uxoqcs, and uxoso. (b) ensure compliance with a dod military service- and/or ddesb-approved site plans. (c) plan, coordinate, and supervise all on-site munitions response and operational range clearance activities. (d) supervise up to ten uxo teams. (e) assist in the development of required plans (e.g., health and safety plans). (f) review all field reports (e.g., daily reports, audits) and approve uxo team reports. (g) evaluate the risk of movement of uxo or dmm within an mrs or operational range with the uxoso, and provide approval for movement by a uxot when the risk of movement is determined to be acceptable. for reference: uxo-tiiis must be able to: (a) meet the criteria for, and perform the functions of, a uxo-ti and uxo-tii. (c) supervise and perform on-site destruction or demilitarization of mec in place or at a consolidated detonation site. this includes determining where and when it is safe to initiate destruction and when engineering controls are required to mitigate the effects of a detonation. (d) implement an explosives storage plan in accordance with applicable guidance. (e) prepare administrative reports required for munitions responses (e.g., daily uxo team report), operational range clearance activities, and similar operations. (f) develop and implement standard operating procedures and work plans for munitions responses and operational range clearance activities. (g) assist in the preparation of risk and hazard analyses. (h) conduct daily site safety briefings. (i) supervise mec-related activities performed at a site. (j) determine if mdeh, which is not known or suspected to be uxo, is safe to ship and properly documented for transport over ptrs in accordance with technical bulletin 700-2, naval sea systems command instruction 8020.8c, technical order 11a-1-47. (k) package military munitions, commercial explosives, and mdeh that has been determined safe for transport over ptrs. (l) serve as the uxo team leader. uxoqcss must be able to: (b) develop and, on approval, implement the project’s quality control (qc) plan for mec-related activities in accordance with applicable requirements. (c) conduct and document qc audits of mec-related activities for compliance with applicable requirements. (d) identify, document, report, and ensure completion of corrective actions to ensure mec-related activities are in accordance with applicable requirements. (e) ensure compliance with dod military service- and/or ddesb-approved site plans. (f) prepare qc reports. uxosos must be able to: (b) develop and, on approval, implement explosives and health and safety plans and programs in accordance with applicable dod, federal, state, and local requirements. (c) ensure compliance with dod military service- and/or ddesb-approved site plans. (d) analyze the potential risks (e.g., operational, explosives safety, general safety) associated with mec-related activities and develop and implement required mitigating measures. (e) establish and ensure compliance with site-specific explosives safety requirements, including: 1. enforcing personnel limits and explosives safety quantity distance (esqd) arcs for explosive-related operations. 2. conducting, documenting, and reporting the results of safety inspections and ensuring implementation of corrective actions. 3. ensuring protective works and safety equipment within an exclusion zone are used, when required; and operated in accordance with manufacturer’s specifications, applicable ddesb approvals, dod policy, and federal, state, or local statutes, regulations, and codes. (f) ensure that air-monitoring equipment is operated and maintained properly at sites with known or potential airborne contaminants (e.g., cwm sites). (g) evaluate the risk of movement (e.g., consolidation) of mec within an mrs or on an operational range with the suxos, and provide approval for movement by a uxot when the risk of movement is determined to be acceptable. ***job location is guam*** security clearance requirement: none this position is part of our federal solutions team. the federal solutions segment delivers resources to our us government customers that ensure the success of missions around the globe. our intelligent employees drive the state of the art as they provide services and solutions in the areas of defense, security, intelligence, infrastructure, and environmental. we promote a culture of excellence and close-knit teams that take pride in delivering, protecting, and sustaining our nation's most critical assets, from earth to cyberspace. throughout the company, our people are anticipating what’s next to deliver the solutions our customers need now. salary range: $15.68 - $71.30 this position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will continue to be posted for an average of 30 days until a qualified applicant is selected or the position has been cancelled. parsons is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other protected status. we truly invest and care about our employee’s wellbeing and provide endless growth opportunities as the sky is the limit, so aim for the stars! imagine next and join the parsons quest—apply today! parsons is aware of fraudulent recruitment practices. to learn more about recruitment fraud and how to report it, please refer to https://www.parsons.com/fraudulent-recruitment/ .

clearance required after day 1 rtx corporation is an aerospace and defense company that provides advanced systems and services for commercial, military and government customers worldwide. it comprises three industry-leading businesses – collins aerospace systems, pratt & whitney, and raytheon. its 185,000 employees enable the company to operate at the edge of known science as they imagine and deliver solutions that push the boundaries in quantum physics, electric propulsion, directed energy, hypersonics, avionics and cybersecurity. the company, formed in 2020 through the combination of raytheon company and the united technologies corporation aerospace businesses, is headquartered in arlington, va. the following position is to join our rtx corporate, enterprise services team: rtx corporation is seeking an experienced qms (quality management system) auditor to join our enterprise quality audit (eqa) team (2nd party audit). the qms auditor will be responsible for conducting second party qms audits across rtx business units to ensure compliance with 91xx series, iso9001, and other relevant standards. this role will involve identifying areas of strength, opportunities and non-compliance, and reviewing and approving corrective action plans. the ideal candidate will have a strong background in quality assurance within the aerospace, space, and/or defense industries, standards, rtx and business unit policies & procedures, and regulatory and customer requirements across rtx sites. perform formal responsibilities of a lead auditor such as audit planning in conjunction with the eqa audit planner, representing the audit team with site leadership, conducting opening and closing meetings, and daily debriefs with site personnel. ensure that processes, products, and services comply with internal standards, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices. complete and issue detailed audit reports, including findings, non-conformances, and review and approve effective corrective actions and ensure implementation effectiveness. may assist rtx certification bodies during site surveillance and recertification audits, including facilitating audit schedules, logistics, and closure of corrective actions. data analysis: support analysis of audit performance to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement. utilize data analytics to support comprehensive audit preparation and planning based on historical and current performance data. collaboration: work closely with regional leads of the eqa team and ops excellence lead to support the audit schedule, ensuring that sites across rtx are audited per the schedule. foster collaborative relationships with functional and business leaders to promote a transformative quality organization aligned with business objectives. participate in weekly corrective action review board meetings to review and approve/reject formal corrective actions. special audits and assessments: support special audits (e.g., suspensions, major customer complaints, high-risk sites, etc.), independent assessments, and site certifications as required by rtx business units. travel requirements: this position requires 70% travel, both domestically and internationally, and can be located within convenient access to a major airport. depending on audit schedules and auditor home location, this may include some weekend travel. qualifications you must have: typically requires a university degree, or equivalent experience and minimum 5 years prior relevant experience, or an certification (evidence is required) the ability to obtain and maintain a secret u.s. government issued security clearance is required qualifications we prefer: existing aatt (aerospace auditor transition training) certification (evidence is required). certification as an aerospace auditor (aa) or aerospace experienced auditor (aea) (evidence is required) experience planning and coordinating multiple audits simultaneously. working knowledge of etq/ bu corrective actions processes/systems proficiency in presenting audit results and concepts to key stakeholders and executive management. asq certification (cqa, cqe, cqm). existing secret security clearance (for raytheon’s dod contracts). core certification proficiency with audit management software and tools. ability to function effectively without direct supervision. excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills. what we offer : whether you’re just starting out on your career journey or are an experienced professional, we offer a robust total rewards package with compensation; healthcare, wellness, retirement and work/life benefits; career development and recognition programs. some of the benefits we excellence, governance, compliance, and demonstrable cost savings through our itam and itom product portfolios. the role as director, itam and itom services (americas), you will establish the strategic vision and drive the execution of our itam and itom practice across the united states and canada. you will lead a team of senior-level technical consultants and business process consultants (bpcs) while defining practice strategy, market positioning, and competitive differentiation. you will be instrumental in expanding the servicenow itam and itom footprint, establishing delivery excellence as a competitive advantage, cultivating deep customer relationships, and maximizing customer value realization in the asset management and operations domains. what you'll do strategic practice leadership & market positioning define and articulate the strategic direction for itam and itom services across the americas, establishing clear market positioning, competitive differentiation, and long-term growth objectives that align with servicenow's broader business strategy. develop and execute a comprehensive business plan for itam and itom services, forecasting market opportunities, identifying expansion vectors within key customer segments, and establishing measurable kpis to drive practice performance and revenue growth. lead strategic capability development initiatives and establish itam and itom as a recognized thought leader in the industry, positioning servicenow as the preferred partner for enterprise asset optimization and operations excellence. stay informed of itam and itom trends, customer landscape changes, regulatory requirements, and emerging opportunities in it operations and asset governance to shape practice strategy and title: Principal Customer Success Executive - Manufacturing Vertical
body: job description job description the customer success executive—us manufacturing is a senior individual contributor role within the customer excellence group (ceg), responsible for driving customer outcomes, retention, and expansion across a portfolio of high-value us manufacturing accounts. this role carries full accountability for the commercial health and strategic growth of assigned accounts—operating with the ownership mentality of a general manager at the account level. this is not an account-monitoring role. we are looking for a commercially minded operator who has personally driven demonstrable yoy growth within a large portfolio, built trusted executive relationships, and executed cross-functional motions that convert platform adoption into measurable business outcomes. you will serve as the primary post-sales customer executive for your accounts—a strategic advisor to manufacturing cios and senior it leaders—and partner closely with sales, delivery, product, and peer ceg functions to ensure customers realize the full value of their servicenow investment and view us as a long-term digital transformation partner. what you get to do in this role • own account-level commercial performance. drive grr, nrr, and renewal outcomes for your assigned accounts through proactive risk management, downsell prevention, and expansion motions. • engage at the executive level as a strategic advisor. build and maintain trusted relationships with c-suite and senior it stakeholders. co-develop digital transformation strategies with customer executives, positioning servicenow as the strategic platform partner for their modernization and ai agendas. bring relevant industry thought leadership and a consulting mindset to every engagement. your executive presence and credibility at this level must be a proven strength, not an aspiration. • translate customer strategy into a servicenow roadmap. take each customer’s enterprise priorities—modernization, cost-out mandates, ai ambitions—and map them to a phased servicenow roadmap that connects platform capabilities to measurable business outcomes. you bridge the gap between what the c-suite wants to achieve and how the platform gets them there. • run complex transformations in our largest accounts. own governance, delivery excellence, and cross-functional orchestration across multiple business units and concurrent workstreams—defining governance models aligned to business and platform strategy and evolving them as engagements scale. • tell the story through data. deliver compelling executive presentations—both internally and to customers—that articulate the value of servicenow through data-driven narratives. you are equally effective presenting a portfolio review to leadership and standing in front of a customer cio making the case for platform expansion. • drive ai consumption and platform adoption. own ai consumption as a strategic kpi within your accounts. design and execute adoption journeys that convert license entitlements into measurable business outcomes, with a focus on emerging agentic capabilities. • set success metrics and drive value realization. establish clear, measurable success metrics with each customer. regularly review progress, proactively identify risks, and refine business transformation plans to ensure milestones are met and value is realized. work with internal teams and the customer to develop strategies that overcome barriers on the path to outcomes. • champion the voice of the customer. synthesize industry-specific feedback, feature requests, and adoption blockers into structured input for product engineering and roadmap prioritization. stay current on manufacturing industry trends, regulatory environments, and digital transformation priorities shaping your accounts. • operationalize customer health at scale. define and manage operational kpis for your portfolio—adoption, technical health, renewals, customer satisfaction, and expansion. deliver regular reporting on customer health, adoption trends, downsell risk, and advocacy pipeline. leverage ai-enabled tools and platforms to automate insights and drive proactive outreach. qualifications the ideal candidate will have extensive experience leading large-scale digital business transformations, acting as a trusted advisor to both internal and c-level customer executives. you combine deep post-sales expertise with the executive presence to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with manufacturing cios and a bias toward action that turns customer outcomes into revenue outcomes. you will be an expert in governance, strategy, value alignment, and execution across cross-functional teams, with a track record of delivering scalable, repeatable success. your passion for driving customer success at an enterprise scale and your ability to work in complex, dynamic environments will be key to your success in this role. to be successful in this role, you will need • ai driven. experience leveraging or critically evaluating how to integrate ai into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. this may include using ai-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing ai-driven insights, or exploring ai’s potential impact on the function or industry. • educational background. ba/bs or equivalent required; mba or advanced degree preferred. • experience. 10–15 years of experience in management consulting, enterprise saas, senior customer success, or technology-enabled business transformation roles. • strategic account ownership. demonstrated experience operating as the primary post-sales customer success executive—owning the commercial outcomes, adoption trajectory, and renewal health. you drive long-term commercial strategy with a deep understanding of how to grow and protect strategic relationships. • transformational leadership expertise. demonstrated success in running large-scale, strategic account transformations and exceeding business objectives. proven ability to build repeatable processes for scalable execution while maintaining a hands-on approach to ensure critical tasks are completed. • business acumen. exceptional commercial instincts. you think in portfolio economics, understand the interplay between adoption, consumption, and revenue, and can translate customer outcomes into business impact narratives that resonate with finance, sales leadership, and executive sponsors. • executive presence and c-suite engagement. proven ability to engage at the c-suite level—both with customers and internally. direct experience partnering with cios and senior it executives to co-develop digital transformation strategies. you bring gravitas, credibility, and the ability to influence without relying on positional authority. • data storytelling. ability to translate complex adoption metrics, value realization, and portfolio performance into executive-level narratives that drive decisions. • cross-functional collaboration. strong track record building productive relationships across sales, presales, delivery, product, and enablement in matrixed, fast-paced environments. you lead through influence, not org-chart authority. • customer centricity and industry awareness. deep understanding of how manufacturing enterprises operate, what drives their priorities, and where friction lives. you instinctively orient around the customer’s outcomes—anticipating concerns, removing barriers to satisfaction, and ensuring every interaction reinforces servicenow’s position as a trusted partner. title: Staff Security Incident Commander
body: job description the servicenow security organization (sso) the servicenow security organization (sso) delivers world-class, innovative security solutions to reduce risk and protect the company and our customers. we enable our customers to migrate their most sensitive data and workloads to the cloud, accelerating our business so that we are the most trusted saas provider. we create an environment where our employees are proud to work and can make a positive impact. role overview servicenow’s security incident command (sic) team is seeking an experienced senior security incident commander to join our fast-growing team. this role will support the orchestration of incident response strategy and communications during critical information security-related incidents. about the sic team the sic team maintains and executes the major security incidents (msi) lifecycle within servicenow, including preparation, response, and recovery. msis are our most challenging and impactful security incidents which pose active or heightened risk to the company and/or our customers. key value areas are preparing the company for msis through tabletop exercises (ttx), coordination of activity between many response workstream partners, maintenance and development of playbooks and procedures, tracking key msi metrics and facts to keep everyone oriented, and communicating status, milestones, blockers, and critical decisions needed to senior management and executive stakeholders, including the ciso. what you get to do in this role orchestration of response and remediation of incident response for highest criticality security events. take ownership and lead response to critical incidents within the company. establish and mature documentation surrounding protocols and procedures governing the security incident command team. prepare and deliver communications, including executive summaries and incident briefings, to key stakeholders during and after incident response. conduct rapid response, mitigation, and investigations on the highest priority cases impacting servicenow and user data. partner with the team members across multiple regions to drive response and investigations globally. organization and facilitation of scenario-based exercises to test and improve incident management and response strategies. maintenance of existing playbooks and procedures, as well as developing new ones, to further standardize sic and its partners' responses when verifying msis. contribute to the organization and completion of post-incident reviews (pirs) and root cause analyses (rcas) following major security incidents. identify new ways to simplify, integrate, automate and refine the major security incident process to better support internal and title: Service Delivery Manager
body: job description the team service delivery is the backbone of servicenow's customer success strategy in the americas. we manage the governance, performance, and strategic alignment of our global system integrator (si) and service delivery partners ensuring that partner-delivered services meet the highest standards of quality, customer satisfaction, and business outcomes. the service delivery function spans partner capacity planning, contingent worker onboarding, contract management, resource optimization, and end-to-end delivery governance across a large ecosystem of delivery partners serving thousands of customers. as a service delivery manager, you will be part of a team supporting the director, service delivery in executing the regional service delivery strategy and governance frameworks. your focus will be on the tactical, day-to-day oversight and governance of assigned partner engagements, ensuring consistent execution of servicenow standards, quality metrics, and customer outcomes. the role the service delivery manager is responsible for overseeing the performance, quality, and operational health of assigned partners. acting as the primary governance point between servicenow and delivery partner(s) for your assigned portfolio, you ensure partner resources assigned to servicenow engagements are delivered in accordance with agreed service levels, quality standards, contractual commitments, and customer outcome expectations. you monitor service delivery performance, identify risks, drive corrective actions, manage escalations, and provide ongoing visibility into delivery health for leadership. your role serves as the critical accountability layer that makes partner performance predictable, scalable, and aligned to servicenow standards across your assigned partners, regardless of whether they are delivering managed services, outsourced operations, subcontracted services, or project-based engagements. you work closely with the director, service delivery to implement governance processes, contribute to strategic initiatives, and escalate systemic issues that require regional leadership attention. responsibilities partner performance governance serve as the primary servicenow point of contact for assigned partner points of contact; maintaining day-to-day oversight of partner service performance against contracted kpis and slas. monitor service delivery performance across assigned partners, tracking key metrics including quality scores, customer satisfaction, utilization rates, delivery timelines, and cost-per-outcome performance; ensuring that servicenow and its customers are getting excellence in delivery from its partner resources. review delivery quality trends, audit findings, and operational metrics to identify systemic issues, root causes, and opportunities for continuous improvement within assigned portfolio. monitor delivery unit economics and cost-per-outcome performance, ensuring the contracted commercial model (unit-based, outcome-based, or hybrid) tracks to delivered value and flag discrepancies. maintain a dashboard or reporting view of assigned partner health metrics and escalate systemic issues to the director, service delivery for strategic resolution or cross-regional alignment. escalation & corrective action lead delivery escalations across servicenow and partner teams for assigned engagements, driving timely issue resolution and ensuring accountability for remediation plans and service recovery activities. document escalation history, track resolution status, and report escalation trends to the director, service delivery and relevant stakeholders. identify patterns in escalations across assigned partners and recommend process improvements or capability enhancements to the director. partner with customer success teams and account teams to protect customer outcomes and address service delivery risks impacting customer health. onboarding & service transitions own tracking and acceptance of transition and mobilization milestones during partner onboarding or service transitions, including staffing ramp against plan, capability/certification readiness, and transition exit criteria. ensure partner resource skills and certifications align with service demands and customer requirements, tracking ongoing development and readiness. communicate onboarding milestones and status to leadership and document lessons learned from transitions. support the director in partner capacity planning by tracking staffing ramps, utilization, and capability readiness for assigned partners. operational governance & reporting manage the operational governance cadence for assigned partners, including weekly performance check-ins, monthly reviews, and quarterly business review preparation. own capacity and demand management processes for assigned partners, including utilization tracking, variance planning, and periodic reconciliation against contracted volumes. manage the change control process for operational or initiative requests that have contractual implications, engaging commercial management as needed. flag discrepancies between service delivery status and invoicing or milestone payment triggers to commercial and finance stakeholders. produce and maintain performance reporting for assigned partners, providing regular updates to the director and internal leadership stakeholders. identify and implement process improvements in response to changes in tooling, operating model, or service delivery requirements. collaboration & coordination coordinate with other service delivery managers in the region and across geographies on initiative design, sequencing, and rollout to ensure consistency. maintain regular interlock with the global partnerships and channels (gpc) team, ensuring partner performance insights, escalations, and capability needs are escalated appropriately. support the director in implementing regional governance frameworks and standard operating procedures across partner-delivered services. contribute to cross-functional initiatives with commercial management, finance, sales, and customer excellence group to support partner relationship development. qualifications core experience 5+ years of experience in service delivery management, vendor governance, partner performance management, or a related operational role within a global technology or saas environment. demonstrated experience managing partner, vendor, or supplier performance through structured governance frameworks, scorecards, and business reviews. proven ability to manage third-party performance against defined slas and kpis, including escalation and corrective action processes. experience managing partners in a customer success and professional services delivery context. track record of driving continuous improvement and service efficiencies in partner or vendor management environments. operational & functional skills experience designing and maintaining operational documentation, including playbooks and standard operating procedures. strong project and program management capability, with a track record of delivering cross-functional initiatives to agreed timelines. proficiency in performance data analysis and reporting, with the ability to draw actionable conclusions from kpi and operational metrics. experience monitoring and tracking partner resource ongoing development of skills and certifications in line with service demands. demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate across functions and levels of seniority without direct line authority. strong organizational, communication, and presentation skills with ability to clearly articulate performance insights to partner leadership and internal stakeholders. servicenow & domain knowledge knowledge of, or ability to rapidly develop proficiency in, servicenow's platform and products. familiarity with customer success and professional services metrics and post-sales operating models, including nps, utilization, rate cards, and product adoption measures. understanding of professional services delivery models, partner economics, and how partner governance supports customer outcomes. ability to balance customer outcomes, business objectives, and partner performance requirements in a complex operating environment. preferred qualifications experience working within or alongside a partner or managed service delivery model, particularly in a vendor governance or service integration capacity. familiarity with scaled saas operating models, ai native environments, and partner-delivered service motions. experience operating within an organizational transformation or operational improvement program in a post-sales or customer success context. certifications in relevant disciplines (e.g., pmp, itil, csm, copc, supplier management). exposure to ai-enabled or agentic workflow tooling within an operational team environment. experience with india-based or nearshore service delivery models and geographically distributed partner teams. prior experience at servicenow or within the servicenow title: Principal Inbound Product Manager
body: job description about the team our connected customer experiences organization is scaling a portfolio of ai-powered capabilities designed to help customers resolve issues quickly and effectively, with ai increasingly able to complete resolutions without requiring human involvement. these capabilities are core to how servicenow proves that ai can operate reliably at enterprise scale — on our own platform, for our own customers. about the role servicenow is looking for a principal inbound product manager to build the evaluation and feedback backbone that makes our ai-powered support products trustworthy, measurable, and continuously improving. we are investing in building structured mechanism for statistical sampling, human review, or feedback capture that closes the loop back into the product. this role owns enabling that mechanism from the ground up, and applying it consistently across all ai-enabled products in the portfolio. this is an inbound-facing role: your primary customers are the product teams and customer support teams across the organization, and your core deliverable is the evaluation & governance infrastructure, taxonomy, and process that lets every ai feature get measurably better over time. what you'll own end-to-end design of the ai product evaluation ecosystem: automated evals, human-in-the-loop review, and a structured feedback taxonomy applied consistently across the organization's ai-enabled support capabilities. a closed-loop process that converts feedback and review findings into concrete product and model improvements. cross-functional coordination across product, ai/ml engineering, data & telemetry, and ai operations to unify how feedback is captured, reviewed, and actioned. the requirements and prioritization inputs that drive continuous improvement in resolution quality and effectiveness, benefiting both internal support teams and external customers. why this role matters own the foundational trust layer for servicenow's ai-powered support products at a moment when the company is scaling ai features faster than it can currently validate them. shape how servicenow itself, not just our customers — operationalizes responsible, data-driven ai product development, with direct executive visibility. sit at the intersection of product, data science, and operations, with the mandate to build something that doesn't exist today rather than optimize an existing process. high-leverage, cross-functional scope: your work becomes the shared standard every ai feature across the org and measured against. what success looks like a structured evaluation ecosystem (automated evals, human review cadence, feedback taxonomy) live and adopted across all major ai-enabled support products. a functioning closed-loop process, with measurable improvement in resolution quality tied to feedback findings. demonstrated progress toward company-wide goals for ai-driven issue resolution, with feedback insights as a contributing driver. ai product and engineering teams actively using the evaluation framework as part of their standard development cycle, not as an afterthought. qualifications to be successful in this role you have: experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate ai into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. this may include using ai-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing ai-driven insights, or exploring ai's potential impact on the function or industry. 15+ years of product management , with recent hands-on experience building ai agents, ai evaluation, feedback, or quality frameworks for ai/ml-powered products. strong ai product sense, able to reason about measuring ai application performance, failure modes, and quality tradeoffs, not just feature delivery. experience designing structured feedback or evaluation systems: golden datasets, statistical sampling, human-in-the-loop review, or similar. data-driven decision-making, comfortable defining metrics, interpreting telemetry, and using both to prioritize. proven track record leading cross-functional initiatives without direct authority, across product, engineering, data science, and operations. experience in a customer support, service delivery, or similarly operational environment is a plus. excellent stakeholder management and communication skills; able to influence senior leaders and align multiple teams around a shared framework. for positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $221,200 - $387,100 , plus equity (when applicable), body: job description principal strategist - public sector, inspire value - moveworks moveworks is the agentic ai assistant platform that empowers the entire workforce. our platform enables employees to converse with all of their business systems through natural language to quickly find answers and automate tasks. powered by the world's most advanced llms, our proprietary models, and a sophisticated agentic ai platform, we're transforming how work gets done by allowing ai to take initiative, streamline complex workflows, and continuously learn and adapt. moveworks is trusted by over 5.5 million employees at more than 350 of the world’s largest companies, including 10% of the fortune 500, to automate everyday tasks and streamline business operations. recognized on the forbes cloud 100 and ai 50 lists, moveworks was also named one of fast company’s 2025 most innovative companies and inc’s best in business, in the best in innovation category. moveworks was also recognized at microsoft’s 2025 partner of the year and in 2024, received the ai breakthrough award. in december 2025, moveworks was acquired by servicenow, marking a pivotal milestone in our journey to create a single front door to work for all business systems. by combining servicenow’s leading workflow automation with moveworks’ reasoning engine and natural language capabilities, we deliver the ai platform for every person and every workflow. built to go beyond basic summaries to deliver meaningful business impact. together, our ai acts across enterprise systems to turn conversations into completed work. by joining our team, you’ll be at the forefront of the ai transformation, backed by the global scale of servicenow and the agility of a high-growth company. we are looking for world-class talent to help us extend agentic ai to every employee across every corner of the business. come join us! servicenow it all started in sunny san diego, california in 2004 when a visionary engineer, fred luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. fast forward to today — servicenow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative ai-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the fortune 500®. our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. but this is just the beginning of our journey. join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone. as a member of the go-to-market (gtm) team, you will play a strategic role at the center of our company, working with customers to identify the operational, strategic, and financial impact that moveworks ai technology can have on their organizations. in this highly visible role, you will be a key leader in helping grow our business value services function, collaborating with sales teams on our largest and most strategic customers in the federal, state, local, and education/non-profit public sector business, demonstrating to customers a significant value opportunity, return on their investment, and engagement model that positions them for a long-lasting partnership with moveworks agentic generative ai solutions establish feedback loops across the gtm team of moveworks and servicenow that enable us to continually iterate and and scale our value messaging and better together messaging and positioning to the market. qualifications what you bring to the table 6+ years of professional experience, with progressive experience in consultative, strategic, and analytical body: job description the servicenow security organization (sso) the servicenow security organization (sso) delivers world-class, innovative security solutions to reduce risk and protect the company and our customers. we enable our customers to migrate their most sensitive data and workloads to the cloud, accelerating our business so that we are the most trusted saas provider. we create an environment where our employees are proud to work and can make a positive impact this is a hands-on engineering and architecture role within cyber defense engineering (cde), applied to some of the hardest, least-defined problems in cyber defense, protecting a platform trusted by thousands of the world's largest enterprises. you'll operate with minimal direction and broad latitude to set the technical agenda. you'll start by tackling one of the highest-stakes problems in enterprise security today: how do you secure a company's own employees and systems as they adopt ai faster than anyone can govern it? think compromised internal agents, ai copilots that leak sensitive data, and shadow ai tools appearing before any policy exists. you'll architect the threat models, controls, and secure-by-design standards other teams build against, partnering with servicenow's product ai security research team to apply frontier research internally, and you'll be the technical authority and red team practices or solving problems that don't have a name yet. this role is for engineers who want to keep solving cyber defense's hardest, least-defined problems at the frontier of the field, title: Technical Readiness & Communities Director
body: job description customer excellence group — product delivery & innovation role overview servicenow is standing up a dedicated communities of practice function within the customer excellence group (ceg). this function is designed to multiply expertise across 3,400+ practitioners worldwide. the director, community of practice will own the strategy, design, and day-to-day operation of this community ecosystem, scaling ai and technical readiness across every geo and every customer-facing role. this role sits at the convergence of three disciplines - readiness, content standardization, and communities and serves as the amplification layer in the pd&i readiness engine. product experts earn hard-won lessons in the field; the readiness team packages them; you multiply them across ceg so expertise is scaled. you will report to the director of technical readiness and partner closely with geo leadership, product, engineering, and servicenow university to build something ceg has never had: a self-sustaining, accountable system for scaling practitioner expertise at speed. relationship to ceg role & org excellence this role is distinct from, and works in close partnership with, the director, ceg role & org excellence. that role owns role mandates, competency frameworks, and organizational design - defining what roles exist across ceg and what they are accountable for. this role owns the community operating model -how practitioners build, share, and apply expertise within those roles once they are defined. you will define the competency framework, and you will keep community programming aligned as role mandates evolve. key responsibilities community strategy and governance define the community operating model, charter, and success metrics for all communities of practice across ceg- scoped to how practitioners engage and share expertise, not organizational role design or reporting structure design and implement community types mapped to certification roles/personas. build the cadence, rituals, and contribution mechanisms (community governance) that keep each community healthy, productive, and self-sustaining over time. establish community health dashboards with leading and lagging indicators—participation rates, content contribution velocity, certification correlation, and practitioner engagement scores practitioner engagement and relationship building recruit, develop, and support geo community practice leaders- practitioner-facing roles distinct from geo business leads who embody the practice at the regional level, dedicating approximately two days per month to community leadership cultivate a global network of practitioner champions who co-author best practices, peer-review, technical readiness and serve as closed feedback loop chairs. build trusted partnerships across geo leaders, product leadership, and pd&i to ensure communities are co-owned rather than centrally imposed partner with the director, ceg role & org excellence to ensure community programming reflects current role mandates and competency frameworks as they evolve maintain an active feedback loop so field lessons flow all the way back to product, informing the next release cycle ai readiness and technical enablement at scale embed ai adoption frameworks, use cases, and best practices into every community channel—making ai readiness a natural part of practitioner workflow, not a separate training event partner with ai architects and the product excellence team to translate technical complexity into community-ready content - adoption frameworks, value realization playbooks, executive briefing guides, and implementation patterns leverage ai-powered tools (yoodli simulations, ai-assisted expertise registries, automated field-voice reporting) to scale community operations without proportional headcount stay current with ai developments across the industry- not just servicenow products - and bring external perspectives into community programming content and knowledge amplification operate the fan-out layer of the readiness engine—taking packaged expertise from pd&i and distributing it through communities so a single asset reaches hundreds of practitioners coordinate with the content standardization lead to ensure community-generated content meets quality, structure, and voice standards contribute to the repository and discovery mechanisms for community-sourced learning assets, playbooks, and field-tested patterns community adoption and behavior change you will partner with the director of ceg field readiness to lead the adoption and behavior change required to make communities of practice stick. build the executive narrative that makes the value of communities visible and repeatable- linking community health to certification rates, time-to-proficiency, customer outcomes, and revenue impact present community strategy, progress, and impact to svp/vp-level audiences, including ceg leadership and cross-functional stakeholders champion a culture where peer-led learning is valued alongside formal training - making the 70-20-10 model real rather than aspirational measurement and continuous improvement define and track metrics across four dimensions: learning metrics (completion, certification velocity), engagement metrics (monthly active contributors, peer participation), business impact (ai attach rates, implementation cycle time, csat), and community sustainability (self-sustaining contribution rates, champion readiness) run quarterly capability reviews with skills gap analysis to ensure community programming stays ahead of role evolution report monthly on community health, course correct quickly, and scale what works critical skills and competencies relationship building you build trust quickly across levels and functions. you know that community adoption depends on relationships - not mandates - and you have a track record of earning co-ownership from regional leaders in matrixed organizations. presentation and executive communication you present strategy, data, and impact to vp/svp audiences with clarity and confidence. you tailor your message to the room whether that is a geo all-hands, a leadership review, or a practitioner workshop. influence without authority you drive outcomes through persuasion, credibility, and coalition-building rather than positional power. you have led practitioner-facing initiatives at enterprise scale where success depended on getting buy-in from leaders who did not report to you - distinct from formal organizational design authority. technical community leadership you have built, scaled, or operated technical communities of practice in large organizations. you understand the mechanics of healthy communities: cadence, rituals, governance, contribution incentives, and sustainability planning. ai fluency and applied ai experience you are a practitioner of ai - not just an observer. you use ai tools daily, understand adoption barriers, and can credibly lead ai readiness programming for technical and customer-facing roles. experience with ai enablement, ai-powered learning platforms, or ai adoption frameworks is essential. change management at scale you have led adoption and behavior-change initiatives that stuck - not just launched. you understand resistance patterns, executive sponsorship models, incentive alignment, and the difference between communication plans and real change management. this is distinct from enterprise organizational design or role architecture, which sits with a separate ceg function. enablement focus/ learning design sensibility you do not need to be an instructional designer or a master trainer, but you do understand adult learning frameworks (70-20-10, bloom’s taxonomy, spaced repetition) well enough to ensure community programming reinforces rather than duplicates formal learning paths. you have experience with skills and competency frameworks. data-driven decision making you define success metrics before you launch, track leading indicators, and course correct based on evidence. you can build and present dashboards that make community health visible to leadership. qualifications required 10+ years of experience in enablement, community management, learning and development, or technical program management in enterprise technology organizations 5+ years leading communities of practice, centers of excellence, or practitioner networks at scale (500+ participants across multiple regions) 2+ years of direct experience with ai technologies - either enabling ai adoption across organizations, building ai-powered learning or enablement programs, or leading technical communities focused on ai/ml capabilities demonstrated success building community programs from scratch in large, matrixed organizations -including defining governance, recruiting volunteer leaders, and sustaining engagement beyond the initial launch experience presenting strategy and results to vp/svp-level audiences with measurable business impact track record of leading change management initiatives that produced durable behavior change - not just awareness campaigns bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience preferred experience building technical certification programs experience at a top-tier enterprise technology company (saas, cloud, platform) in a customer success, professional services, or post-sale organization familiarity with servicenow products, the now platform, or the servicenow ecosystem experience with ai-powered enablement tools (e.g., conversation intelligence, ai coaching simulations, adaptive learning platforms) certifications or formal training in change management (prosci, adkar) or community management (cmx, community roundtable) experience operating hub-and-spoke enablement models across global geos degree in organizational development, learning
